backlog.spec: Add all rdkit.Chem.Descriptors.descList descriptors (computed per molecule, nan_to_num, clip to +-1e6) concatenated with the Morgan bits as features for the random forest. Keep other settings unchanged.
backlog.title: RDKit 2D descriptors + RF

backlog.spec: Replace the RF with LightGBM (n_estimators 800, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 31, colsample_bytree 0.5, subsample 0.8 with subsample_freq 1, n_jobs 8, random_state seed) on RDKit 2D descriptors plus Crippen/MolLogP, using nan_to_num and clipping.
backlog.title: Descriptors only LightGBM

backlog.spec: Switch Morgan features to count fingerprints via GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy with radius 3 and 2048 bits, keep RF.
backlog.title: Count Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: Use CatBoostRegressor (iterations 1500, depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, loss MAE or RMSE, thread_count 8, random_seed seed, verbose 0) on RDKit descriptors plus count Morgan radius 2 with 1024 bits.
backlog.title: Descriptors + counts into CatBoost

backlog.spec: Average predictions of RF (on fingerprints+descriptors), LightGBM and CatBoost on the same feature matrix. Equal weights.
backlog.title: Ensemble RF + LightGBM + CatBoost

backlog.spec: Train LightGBM with objective huber (alpha 1.0) instead of L2 on descriptor+fingerprint features, since the metric is MAE.
backlog.title: MAE/Huber objective for GBM

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForest with ExtraTreesRegressor (500 trees, max_features 0.3, min_samples_leaf 1) on fingerprints+descriptors.
backlog.title: Extra trees

backlog.spec: Append the 167 MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) to the features of the existing pipeline.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys

backlog.spec: Concatenate Morgan counts with atom-pair count fingerprints (1024 bits) and topological torsion counts (1024 bits) from rdFingerprintGenerator; use with LightGBM.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and torsion count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Add functional-class Morgan fingerprints (GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen, radius 3, 1024 bits, counts) to the ECFP features.
backlog.title: Feature-Morgan (FCFP) added

backlog.spec: Implement SVR (sklearn, kernel precomputed) with a Tanimoto/MinMax kernel on Morgan count fingerprints, C=5, epsilon 0.1; compute kernel with numpy.
backlog.title: SVR with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Fit KernelRidge with precomputed MinMax kernel on count fingerprints (alpha 0.5), average with the RF predictions 50/50.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge Tanimoto + RF blend

backlog.spec: Closed-form GP regression with MinMax kernel on count Morgan, noise 0.3, mean-centered targets; return posterior mean.
backlog.title: Gaussian process on Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: sklearn MLPRegressor (256,128 hidden, early_stopping, alpha 1e-3) on QuantileTransformer/standard-scaled descriptors; bag 5 seeds and average.
backlog.title: MLP on descriptors

backlog.spec: Set MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF=2, MAX_FEATURES=0.2 and N_TREES=500 for the RF.
backlog.title: RF min_samples_leaf and max_features tuning

backlog.spec: Drop fingerprint columns that are active in fewer than 5 training molecules before fitting, applied consistently to test.
backlog.title: Remove low-variance bits

backlog.spec: Add features: sums of Crippen atomic logP contributions binned by atom-type (rdMolDescriptors._CalcCrippenContribs, summed per type index) plus total MolLogP and TPSA, MR, to the fingerprints.
backlog.title: Crippen contributions per-atom features

backlog.spec: Fit the model to y minus MolLogP (Crippen) as target, then add MolLogP back to predictions; use RF/LightGBM on fingerprints+descriptors.
backlog.title: Residual learning on Crippen logP

backlog.spec: Preprocess SMILES: keep the largest fragment (rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser) and neutralize charges (Uncharger) before featurization.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and neutralization

backlog.spec: Add SMARTS-count features for carboxylic acid, aliphatic amine, amidine, sulfonamide, phenol, tetrazole, quaternary N, and pyridine-like N, appended to the features.
backlog.title: Ionizable group counts

backlog.spec: XGBRegressor (hist, n_estimators 1000, learning_rate 0.03, max_depth 6, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.4, reg:absoluteerror) on descriptors + Morgan counts.
backlog.title: XGBoost on mixed features

backlog.spec: Train 5 LightGBM models with different seeds and feature subsamples and average them for lower variance.
backlog.title: Multi-seed bagging of GBM

backlog.spec: Within fit_predict, create 5-fold inner out-of-fold predictions for RF, LightGBM, and SVR-Tanimoto; fit a non-negative linear regression on them and apply to the test predictions.
backlog.title: Stacking with ridge meta-learner

backlog.spec: LightGBM with learning_rate 0.01, 3000 trees, num_leaves 15, min_child_samples 10, lambda_l2 5, colsample 0.3 with an inner 10% validation split for early stopping (stopping 100).
backlog.title: Lower learning rate longer GBM

backlog.spec: Use Morgan radius 3 with 4096 bits and chirality enabled in the RF.
backlog.title: Larger radius, bigger bit vector

backlog.spec: Compute Weisfeiler-Lehman-like hashed atom environment features with atom properties (Gasteiger charge, atom logP contribution, aromaticity) pooled via sum and max over atoms into a dense vector; feed to LightGBM with descriptors.
backlog.title: Graph-style message passing features

backlog.spec: Add EState fingerprint sums (rdkit.Chem.EState.Fingerprinter.FingerprintMol, both counts and max-EState arrays) and VSA descriptors to the feature set.
backlog.title: Gasteiger-charge descriptors (EState)

backlog.spec: Clip training targets to the 1st and 99th percentiles before fitting to reduce the influence of outliers on the MAE.
backlog.title: Target winsorizing

backlog.spec: Instead of the mean of trees, return the median of per-tree predictions from the RF (np.median over estimators_ predictions), aimed at MAE.
backlog.title: Median-of-trees RF prediction

backlog.spec: Weight each training molecule by 1/sqrt(count of its Murcko scaffold in the training set) when fitting, to improve generalization to unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Sample-weights by scaffold frequency

backlog.spec: Add a module-level dict keyed by SMILES string that stores the per-molecule feature row (Morgan bits plus clipped descriptors) and the Crippen logP. featurize() and crippen() look up cached values and compute only missing ones. This cuts the repeated descriptor cost over the 15 fits and frees time budget for other additions. Predictions are unchanged, so it is safe to combine with later ideas.
backlog.title: Cache featurization across folds

backlog.spec: Add a fourth base model: SVR with precomputed MinMax kernel (sum of min / sum of max) on atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048, count vector). Compute the features inside featurize into a separate array and keep it out of the tree inputs. Add its column to base_preds and the inner OOF array (shape 4 columns) so the positive linear meta-learner weighs it. Use C=5, epsilon=0.1.
backlog.title: Atom-pair count fingerprint SVR as 4th stack member

backlog.spec: Add KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=0.3) on the Morgan Tanimoto kernel as an extra stack column (on the Crippen residual). It is cheap, and its smooth predictions differ from those of SVR. Update the OOF array to 4 columns.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge Tanimoto base model

backlog.spec: In base_preds, replace the single LightGBM with the average of 3 LightGBM models using different seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2), each with subsample 0.8 and colsample 0.3. Keep it as one stack column. This reduces variance of the boosted model.
backlog.title: Multi-seed LightGBM bagging inside stack

backlog.spec: For the ExtraTrees stack column, predict with the per-sample median across estimators_ instead of the mean (np.median over [t.predict(X) for t in et.estimators_]). Apply this to both the OOF and the final predictions. Median is robust to outliers and fits the MAE metric.
backlog.title: Median-of-trees ExtraTrees

backlog.spec: After computing y = train_y - crippen, clip y to its 1st and 99th percentiles of the training set before fitting all base models and the meta-learner. Predictions are not clipped. This reduces the pull of outlying Crippen errors on the fits.
backlog.title: Winsorize residual targets

backlog.spec: Append about 12 SMARTS-match counts to the descriptor block: carboxylic acid, aliphatic amine (primary, secondary, tertiary), amidine/guanidine, sulfonamide NH, tetrazole, phenol, quaternary N, pyridine-like N, and nitro. Use Chem.MolFromSmarts with GetSubstructMatches. These capture ionization, which drives logD and is poorly represented in fingerprints. Only the tree models see them, since the SVR uses the first N_BITS columns.
backlog.title: Ionizable group count features

backlog.spec: Replace the plain Crippen subtraction with a linear baseline. Fit a Ridge (alpha 1) on about 10 descriptors (MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, FractionCSP3, NumRotatableBonds, and ring count) using the training set. Use its prediction as the baseline to subtract and add back. Within each fit, fit the baseline on the full training set, and the same baseline for the inner OOF.
backlog.title: Second physics baseline: blend Crippen with fitted linear correction

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule (MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles). Give each molecule the weight 1/sqrt(scaffold count). Pass the weights as sample_weight to ExtraTrees, LightGBM and SVR (SVR.fit takes sample_weight with a precomputed kernel). This counters overrepresented scaffolds, which fits the scaffold-split evaluation.
backlog.title: Sample weights by scaffold rarity

backlog.spec: Keep the tree features as they are. For the SVR Tanimoto kernel, build separate binary Morgan fingerprints with radius 3 and 4096 bits, stored in a separate array. Compute the kernel on these instead of the first N_BITS columns. Everything else stays the same.
backlog.title: Larger-radius Morgan hashed to 4096 bits for the kernel only

backlog.spec: Add a module-level dict keyed by SMILES string that stores the per-molecule feature row (Morgan bits plus clipped descriptors) and the Crippen logP. featurize() and crippen() look up the cache and compute only missing molecules. Nothing else changes. This cuts the runtime so that more stack members fit within 10 minutes. Expect the score to stay about the same.
backlog.title: Cache featurization across folds

backlog.spec: Add a fourth base model: SVR with a precomputed MinMax kernel on hashed atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 2048, GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). MinMax kernel is sum(min)/sum(max), computed in chunks. C=5, epsilon=0.1. Fit it on the Crippen residual. Extend base_preds and the OOF matrix to 4 columns so the positive LinearRegression meta-learner weights it. Cache the fingerprints.
backlog.title: Atom-pair count SVR as 4th stack member

backlog.spec: Add sklearn KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=0.3) on the existing Tanimoto kernel of the Morgan bits as a 4th column in base_preds. It is cheap, and its errors differ from SVR's epsilon-insensitive fit. The meta-learner is the existing positive linear regression.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge on Tanimoto as stack member

backlog.spec: In base_preds, replace the single LGBMRegressor with the average of 3 LightGBM models using seeds seed, seed+1 and seed+2 (subsample 0.8, colsample 0.3). This lowers GBM variance before stacking. Keep all other hyperparameters the same.
backlog.title: Multi-seed LightGBM bagging

backlog.spec: Compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule (MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles). Weight each sample by 1/sqrt(count of its scaffold in the training set), normalized to mean 1. Pass sample_weight to ExtraTrees, LightGBM and SVR (SVR via sample_weight in fit). Since test folds contain unseen scaffolds, this reduces overfit to the common scaffolds.
backlog.title: Scaffold-rarity sample weights

backlog.spec: Extend the meta-learner input to [oof predictions, constant column] and fit with Ridge(alpha=1) allowing an intercept. Also add the residual-target mean shrinkage. Alternatively add the raw Crippen logP as a fourth meta feature so the stack can rescale the physics baseline. The final prediction is meta.predict(base) + cte as now. Check that the weights stay sensible.
backlog.title: Second-level meta with Crippen as input

backlog.spec: Replace the raw Crippen subtraction with a fitted baseline. Fit Ridge on a small set of descriptors (MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, FractionCSP3, and the 12 count of ionizable groups from SMARTS) on the training fold only. Use its prediction as the baseline in place of Crippen. The tree models learn the residual, and the baseline is added back. Compute it inside fit_predict so there is no leakage.
backlog.title: Linear-corrected physics baseline

backlog.spec: Append hashed atom-pair count fingerprints (1024 bits) and topological-torsion count fingerprints (1024 bits) from rdFingerprintGenerator to the feature matrix used by ExtraTrees and LightGBM only. The SVR keeps its Morgan columns, which are first in the matrix. Log1p-transform the counts.
backlog.title: Atom-pair and torsion count features for ExtraTrees

backlog.spec: After featurizing the train set, compute the bit column sums over the Morgan block, and keep only bits set in at least 3 training molecules plus all descriptor columns. Apply the same mask to the test features. Keep the Tanimoto kernel on the original unmasked bits. This reduces noise features for ExtraTrees (max_features=0.3) and speeds the job up.
backlog.title: Drop rare fingerprint bits

backlog.spec: Replace the positive LinearRegression meta-learner with a non-negative least absolute deviation fit. Minimize mean |y - oof @ w| with scipy.optimize.minimize (method SLSQP, w>=0, start at 1/3 each). The metric is MAE, so this fits the loss directly. Leave the base models unchanged.
backlog.title: Stack-level target noise robustness: MAE-tuned meta

backlog.spec: In base_preds, pass sample_weight to ExtraTrees, LightGBM and SVR (SVR.fit supports sample_weight). Compute the weights inside fit_predict from the training SMILES: take the Murcko scaffold of each molecule (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles) and set w = 1/sqrt(count of that scaffold in the training set), then normalize to mean 1. Pass the weights through the inner stacking folds by indexing them with tr. The aim is to stop the big scaffold clusters from dominating, since the test folds hold unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Scaffold-rarity sample weights

backlog.spec: Add sklearn KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha=0.3) fit on the Tanimoto kernel of the Morgan bits, as a 4th column in base_preds. It reuses the kernel matrix already computed for the SVR, so it costs almost nothing. Change the oof array to 4 columns. Keep the non-negative linear meta-learner.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge Tanimoto as 4th stack member

backlog.spec: Replace the plain Crippen residual with a fitted baseline. Fit a Ridge regression (alpha 1) on the training set using [Crippen logP, TPSA, MolWt, HBD count, HBA count, fraction of sp3 carbons, and the 8 ionizable-group counts], standardized. Use the out-of-fold ridge prediction as the baseline, so the residual targets aren't leaked. Fit the final ridge on all training data for the test baseline. The trees, LightGBM and SVR then fit y minus this baseline. Add the baseline back at the end.
backlog.title: Linear-corrected Crippen baseline

backlog.spec: After featurizing, compute the column sums of the Morgan bit block on the training matrix. Keep only bits set in at least 5 training molecules, and always keep the descriptor and group columns. Apply the same column mask to the test matrix. The mask applies to the ExtraTrees and LightGBM inputs. The SVR kernel can use the masked bits too. This reduces noise features and speeds up the fits.
backlog.title: Drop rare and constant fingerprint bits

backlog.spec: Compute a separate radius-3, 4096-bit Morgan bit fingerprint, used only for the Tanimoto-SVR kernel. ExtraTrees and LightGBM keep the existing features. Add this block to the cached feature matrix, or compute it in a separate function with a per-SMILES cache. Slice it in base_preds for the SVR.
backlog.title: Kernel-only larger Morgan for SVR

backlog.spec: Add a 4th stack member: SVR(kernel='rbf', C=3, epsilon=0.1, gamma='scale') on the RDKit descriptor and group columns. Preprocess them with a QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal', n_quantiles=200) fitted on the training fold. This gives the stack a model whose errors differ from the fingerprint models. Use 4 oof columns.
backlog.title: Add RBF-kernel SVR on scaled descriptors

backlog.spec: Replace the LinearRegression(positive=True) meta-learner with a non-negative weight vector found by scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP). Minimize the mean absolute error of oof @ w against y, with w >= 0 and sum(w) = 1, starting from equal weights. Predict with base_preds @ w. This matches the MAE loss and resists outliers.
backlog.title: Meta-learner trained with MAE

backlog.spec: Raise the final ExtraTrees to 1500 trees, with max_features=0.3 and min_samples_leaf=1. Keep 200 trees in the inner stacking folds. This lowers the variance of the main base model at small cost. Also set bootstrap=False explicitly.
backlog.title: Repeated-seed ExtraTrees with bigger forest

backlog.spec: After fitting the stacked model once, predict the test SMILES. Then retrain the ExtraTrees and LightGBM base models on the training set plus the test molecules, with their first-pass predictions as targets (residual scale) and sample weight 0.3. Use the retrained models for the final base predictions. Keep the meta weights. This is a self-training step that adapts to unseen scaffolds. Make sure it uses only test SMILES and never test labels.
backlog.title: Pseudo-label augmentation from test molecules

backlog.spec: Add a kNN regressor on the Tanimoto distance (k=5, distance-weighted, brute force, precomputed distances as 1 minus the Tanimoto kernel) as a 4th stack base model, predicting the Crippen residual. It brings local similarity information with a different bias from the other models. The meta-learner weights it automatically.
backlog.title: Neighbor-target feature (kNN residual)

backlog.spec: In base_preds, compute each training molecule's Murcko scaffold (rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, empty string on failure) and weight = 1/sqrt(count of that scaffold in the training set), normalized to mean 1. Pass sample_weight to ExtraTreesRegressor.fit and LGBMRegressor.fit (SVR fit also accepts sample_weight). Train scaffolds are disjoint from test scaffolds, so down-weighting common scaffolds may improve generalization. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Scaffold-rarity sample weights

backlog.spec: Add two dense features to the ExtraTrees and LightGBM inputs: the Tanimoto-weighted mean of the Crippen-residual targets of the 5 most similar training molecules, and the max Tanimoto similarity. For training rows, compute them leave-one-out (exclude self, and ideally exclude same-scaffold neighbors) from the Morgan bit matrix using the existing tanimoto function. For test rows use all training molecules. Append them as columns in base_preds.
backlog.title: kNN residual neighbor-target feature

backlog.spec: Replace the non-negative LinearRegression meta-learner with weights found by minimizing mean absolute error of the out-of-fold stacked predictions. Use scipy.optimize.minimize (Powell or SLSQP) over 3 weights with bounds [0,1] and a sum-to-1 normalization, starting from equal weights. This matches the MAE loss.
backlog.title: MAE-fitted meta-learner

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, replace the random inner KFold used to build the out-of-fold stack predictions with GroupKFold, grouped by Murcko scaffold (generic scaffold string mapped to integer ids). This makes the OOF predictions mimic the unseen-scaffold evaluation, so the meta weights are better calibrated. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Scaffold-grouped inner stacking folds

backlog.spec: Compute a second fingerprint, a Morgan count vector with radius 3 and 4096 bits, only for the Tanimoto-SVR. Use the MinMax kernel on counts (sum of min over sum of max, computed in chunks with numpy) instead of the bit Tanimoto. ExtraTrees and LightGBM keep the current features. Cache the matrix per SMILES to save time.
backlog.title: Bigger-radius Morgan for the SVR kernel only

backlog.spec: After subtracting Crippen, fit the base models on the residual as now, but shrink large residuals with a soft clip such as r' = sign(r)*min(|r|, 1.5 + 0.3*(|r|-1.5)) for |r|>1.5, and invert nothing (it only damps outliers). This differs from hard percentile clipping and is aimed at MAE. Apply it to the targets for all three base models and the meta learner.
backlog.title: Quantile-transformed target with MAE-aware blend

backlog.spec: Give LightGBM only the dense features (RDKit descriptors plus group counts) and a 256-bit folded Morgan fingerprint rather than all 2048 bits. Keep ExtraTrees and SVR unchanged. This should diversify the stack members and cut LightGBM's time. Implement it by slicing columns of Xtr and Xte in base_preds.
backlog.title: Per-model feature subsetting

backlog.spec: Add a fourth base model: ExtraTreesRegressor (300 trees, max_features 0.5, min_samples_leaf 2) trained only on the dense columns (descriptors and group counts, no fingerprint bits). The stack then has 4 columns, so oof needs 4 columns and the meta-learner sees them. Its errors should be less correlated with the fingerprint models.
backlog.title: Extra stack member: ExtraTrees on descriptors only

backlog.spec: The count of atom-order-dependent features is small, so instead augment the training set: for each training molecule add one extra row whose descriptor features are the same and whose Morgan fingerprint uses a Morgan generator with a different random bit hash. Skip this if it is not meaningful. Simpler alternative: bag ExtraTrees over 3 different max_features values (0.2, 0.3, 0.5) and average them as one stack member. Implement the bagging alternative.
backlog.title: Test-time augmentation by randomized SMILES atom order

backlog.spec: After the meta-learner prediction, fit a small LightGBM (100 trees, depth 3, lr 0.05) on the out-of-fold stacked residual (y minus the meta prediction on OOF) using only 20 key dense features (MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, HBD, HBA, the 8 group counts, and so on). Add its prediction, scaled by 0.5, to the final output. This tries to correct systematic ionization and polarity errors.
backlog.title: Residual-corrected second-stage on stack error

backlog.spec: In base_preds, compute each training molecule's Murcko scaffold (rdkit MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, cached per SMILES), count scaffold frequency in the training set, and pass sample_weight = 1/sqrt(count) (normalized to mean 1) to ExtraTrees.fit and LGBMRegressor.fit, and to SVR.fit. Since test folds hold unseen scaffolds, this reduces over-weighting of big congeneric series. Leave the meta-learner unchanged.
backlog.title: Scaffold-rarity sample weights

backlog.spec: Replace LinearRegression(positive=True) meta-learner with weights found by minimizing mean absolute error of oof @ w over the simplex-like constraint w>=0 using scipy.optimize.minimize (SLSQP, start at equal weights 1/3, bounds (0,2)), no intercept. The loss is MAE so the blend should be fit for MAE directly.
backlog.title: MAE-fitted meta-learner

backlog.spec: Instead of subtracting raw MolLogP, fit a Ridge (alpha 1) on the training fold using [MolLogP, MolMR, TPSA, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, fraction of carboxylic acids and basic amines from GROUPS counts] to predict y, and use its prediction as baseline for residuals (trained on the full training set; in the inner OOF loop reuse the same baseline for simplicity). Add the baseline back at predict time.
backlog.title: Linear-corrected Crippen baseline

backlog.spec: After the stack is fit, predict the test molecules, then refit the ExtraTrees and LightGBM members with the test molecules added as extra training rows carrying their stack predictions as targets (sample weight 0.3), and predict test again with the same meta weights. Only the final base_preds call is repeated; no inner CV redo.
backlog.title: Pseudo-label self-training with test molecules

backlog.spec: Train base models on a monotone-transformed Crippen residual: r = y - crippen; fit a QuantileTransformer(output_distribution='normal') on training r (scaled by the training std back to original units), fit stack on transformed values, and invert the transform on the meta predictions before adding Crippen. Uses sklearn only.
backlog.title: Quantile-transformed target

backlog.spec: No change to training. For test molecules only, no augmentation is meaningful for canonical fingerprints, so instead augment training: add a second copy of every training molecule built from a randomized atom-order SMILES (Chem.MolToSmiles(m, doRandom=True) with seeded random state via random.seed) before featurization. Since Morgan and descriptors are order-invariant, instead use this for bagging: train ExtraTrees on bootstrap resamples (max_samples=0.8, bootstrap=True) with 500 trees to add variance reduction and diversity.
backlog.title: Test-time SMILES augmentation for fingerprints

backlog.spec: Change the SVR kernel to the average of the Tanimoto kernel on Morgan bits and an RBF kernel on standardized RDKit descriptors (QuantileTransformer-normal scaled, gamma=1/n_features). Keep precomputed SVR with C=5. This gives the third stack member descriptor information while keeping it distinct from the trees.
backlog.title: Per-model feature subsetting: SVR on Morgan+groups kernel mix

backlog.spec: After the stack prediction, compute the OOF stack residuals on training molecules, then for each test molecule add 0.5 * Tanimoto-weighted mean (weights = sim^3, top 5 neighbours with sim>0.5) of the neighbours' OOF residuals; if no neighbours exceed 0.5, add nothing. Use the OOF predictions from the existing inner loop and the meta weights.
backlog.title: Gaussian-process-style kNN residual stage

backlog.spec: Change the LightGBM member to boosting_type='dart', n_estimators=500, learning_rate=0.05, num_leaves=15, drop_rate=0.1, colsample_bytree=0.2, reg_lambda=5, min_child_samples=15. Keeps the other members unchanged; aims for a more diverse, better-regularized boosting member.
backlog.title: Deeper LightGBM with dart and strong regularization

backlog.spec: Memoize per-SMILES features in a module-level dict so each molecule is featurized once. Append 1024-bit atom-pair and 1024-bit topological-torsion count fingerprints (log1p-transformed) to the feature matrix used by ExtraTrees and LightGBM only. The SVR keeps using the first N_BITS Morgan columns. Keep the rest of the stack unchanged.
backlog.title: Atom-pair/torsion counts plus cached features combined

backlog.spec: Replace the inner KFold(5, shuffle) used to build out-of-fold predictions for the meta-learner with GroupKFold, grouped by Murcko scaffold SMILES of the training molecules. Generic scaffolds are fine for molecules with no rings. This makes the stack weights reflect the unseen-scaffold test condition, so they should favour the models that generalise better.
backlog.title: Scaffold-grouped inner stacking folds

backlog.spec: After the first stacked prediction on test_smiles, add the test molecules to the training set with their predicted Crippen residuals as targets. Give them sample weight 0.3. Refit ExtraTrees and LightGBM on the augmented set and predict the test molecules again. Average this prediction with the first one. Use the same stack weights as before. This is transductive and does not use test labels.
backlog.title: Pseudo-label self-training with test molecules

backlog.spec: For the Morgan fingerprint part, enumerate no extra variants. Instead, add augmentation by ring-perturbed conformer-free features: compute the Morgan fingerprint with useChirality=True and with useBondTypes=False as two extra 512-bit blocks appended to the ExtraTrees and LightGBM features. This gives the trees alternate views of the same structure.
backlog.title: Randomized-SMILES test-time augmentation

backlog.spec: Switch the stacked LightGBM to boosting_type='dart', with 300 trees, learning_rate 0.08, drop_rate 0.1, num_leaves 15, min_child_samples 15, reg_lambda 5, colsample_bytree 0.3 and subsample 0.7. Keep the other stack members. Use the same seed. Check that run time stays within the limit.
backlog.title: Dart LightGBM with strong regularization

backlog.spec: Change the SVR kernel to 0.7*Tanimoto(Morgan bits) + 0.3*RBF on standardized (quantile-scaled) descriptors, with gamma=1/n_features. It is a precomputed kernel. Compute the descriptor scaler on the training fold only. Keep C=5 and epsilon=0.1. This gives the SVR physico-chemical information alongside the substructure similarity.
backlog.title: Per-model kernel mix for SVR

backlog.spec: After the stacked prediction, compute out-of-fold stack residuals on the training set from the inner CV. For each test molecule, take the Tanimoto-weighted mean (sim^3, top 5 neighbours with sim>0.6) of the neighbours' OOF residuals. Add 0.5 times it to the prediction. Do nothing when no neighbours qualify.
backlog.title: Second-stage residual correction with kNN

backlog.spec: Make the meta-learner a non-negative LinearRegression with an intercept over the three base predictions. Add the products of each prediction with the standardized Crippen logP, which lets the weights depend on lipophilicity. Fit with a Ridge (alpha 1) instead, and clip the final output to the range of the training targets plus 0.5.
backlog.title: Monotone-constrained stack with intercept and Crippen interaction

backlog.spec: After the stack is fit, train a small ExtraTrees (200 trees, min_samples_leaf 3, max_features 0.3) on the inner OOF stack residuals. Use the same features. Add 0.5 times its prediction to the test output. This corrects systematic structure-dependent bias in the stack.
backlog.title: Boosting-on-residuals second ExtraTrees

backlog.spec: After fitting ExtraTrees, replace each test prediction with the weighted median of the training targets over the leaf co-members. To do this, use et.apply to get leaf indices. For each test row, gather the training targets that share a leaf in each tree, pooling them across trees, then take the median. Use this as the ET stack member to suit the MAE metric. Keep it vectorized and limit it to 200 trees to control the cost.
backlog.title: Huber-loss ExtraTrees via leaf median refit

backlog.spec: Combine two near-miss ideas on the incumbent. Append 1024-bit hashed atom-pair and 1024-bit topological-torsion count fingerprints (log1p) to the features used by ExtraTrees and LightGBM, and keep the Morgan bits alone for the Tanimoto SVR. Also fit all base models and the stack on the quantile-normal transformed Crippen residual, and invert the transform on the final prediction. Cache features per SMILES in a dict so the 15 fits don't recompute them.
backlog.title: Atom-pair/torsion counts plus quantile-normal target combined

backlog.spec: In fit_predict, after the first stacked prediction on test_smiles, append the test molecules with their predicted residuals to the training set. Use sample weight 0.3 for them. Refit only the final ExtraTrees and LightGBM on the augmented set (skip the inner stacking loop and reuse the stack weights already fitted). Return the stacked prediction from the refit models. Keep the 200-tree inner settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Pseudo-label self-training with test molecules

backlog.spec: At prediction time, build 5 extra copies of each test molecule by randomizing atom order (Chem.MolToSmiles with doRandom=True, seeded via np.random/RDKit random seed from seed). Featurize each copy and run the final base models on it. Average the stacked predictions over the original and the copies. Fingerprints are invariant, but descriptors and group counts may shift slightly, so it is mostly a variance-reduction check. Training stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Randomized-SMILES test-time augmentation

backlog.spec: After the stack, compute out-of-fold stacked predictions on the training set from the inner folds (the oof matrix times the meta weights). Fit a small ExtraTrees (200 trees, min_samples_leaf 5, max_features 0.3) on the descriptors and group columns to predict the remaining residual y minus the oof stack. Add 0.5 times its test prediction to the final output.
backlog.title: Second-stage ExtraTrees on stack residuals

backlog.spec: Replace the LinearRegression(positive=True, fit_intercept=False) meta-learner with a small LightGBM meta-learner (num_leaves 4, 100 trees, lr 0.05, min_child_samples 40). Its inputs are the 3 oof predictions plus raw Crippen logP. Constrain the 3 model columns to monotone increasing with monotone_constraints. Fit it on the oof matrix. Predict from the test base predictions plus Crippen.
backlog.title: Monotone stack with intercept and per-model Crippen interaction

backlog.spec: Add a stack member that is an ExtraTrees classifier or regressor trained on a different target. The target is the clipped residual in [-1.5, 1.5] with sample weights 1. Its output is added as a fourth oof column. The idea is that a bounded-target forest is robust to outliers and adds diversity. Keep it to 200 trees and reuse the cached features.
backlog.title: Multi-task auxiliary targets from Crippen residual sign

backlog.spec: Instead of one ExtraTrees fit on all the data, fit 8 ExtraTrees of 100 trees each. Each is trained on a bootstrap that resamples whole Butina or Murcko-scaffold clusters (sample scaffolds with replacement) rather than molecules. Average them as the ExtraTrees stack column. This regularizes toward generalizing to unseen scaffolds.
backlog.title: Scaffold-aware cluster bagging

backlog.spec: Within fit_predict, fit a quick LightGBM (200 trees) on the training features. Keep only the top 400 features by gain importance, always including the group counts. Then train ExtraTrees and LightGBM on that subset in the stack. The SVR still uses the full Morgan bits. Compute the selection inside each fit to avoid leakage.
backlog.title: Descriptor feature selection by importance

backlog.spec: Change the stacked LightGBM to use extra_trees=True (randomized split thresholds), lr 0.02 and 1000 trees, num_leaves 15, colsample 0.3, lambda_l2 5, which is a smoother, more regularized boosted model. Everything else stays unchanged. Check that the run time stays under the 10 minute limit.
backlog.title: Boosted ExtraTrees depth schedule via LightGBM with extra_trees

backlog.spec: Replace the raw Crippen baseline with b = Crippen + ridge correction. The correction is fit on the training set with a Ridge (alpha 10) on standardized TPSA, fraction of sp3 carbons, HBD, HBA, number of aromatic rings and the 8 ionizable-group counts, using the target y - Crippen. Use the out-of-fold prediction of this ridge inside the inner folds only. This is cleaner than the earlier in-sample variant that crashed. Then the base models fit y minus this baseline.
backlog.title: Physics baseline blend of Crippen and fitted ridge on few descriptors

cand.description: Cut the extra-trees cost (the bottleneck) by using fewer features per split, fewer trees, and 3 inner folds instead of 5, so the stacked ensemble fits in the 10-minute limit.

incumbent.description: Append 8 ionizable-group SMARTS match counts (carboxylic acid, aliphatic amine, amidine, sulfonamide, phenol, tetrazole, quaternary N, pyridine-like N) to the fingerprint and descriptor features.

memo: Helped: ExtraTrees over RF (0.7230 to 0.5744), the Crippen MolLogP residual (0.5387), the ExtraTrees/LightGBM/Tanimoto-SVR stack (0.5134), and 8 ionizable-group SMARTS counts (0.5042/0.5072, incumbent mean 0.5057). Did not help: MACCS (0.5771), count Morgan (0.5859), EState (0.5147), GP (0.5934), LightGBM alone (0.5530), ExtraTrees tuning (0.5143), Huber LightGBM (0.5154), target clipping (0.5153), dropping nested stacking (0.5211, 0.5204), MAE-fitted stack weights (0.5092), kNN residual features (0.5094). Most variants sit at 0.504 to 0.515, within noise (sd 0.0042). Crashes came from heavy models (CatBoost, MLP, XGBoost, multi-seed LightGBM), probably time or memory limits. Near misses: atom-pair/torsion counts (0.4989/0.5003), quantile-normal residual target (0.4971/0.5040), memoized features (0.4998/0.5026), RBF SVR as 4th member (0.5005/0.5018). Next: combine atom-pair/torsion counts, feature caching and the quantile-normal target on the incumbent, then replicate. Keep runtime and memory low. Avoid heavy models and ideas already tried.
